narration.text: Alaska's financial-responsibility and mandatory-insurance laws aim to protect road users from uninsured drivers. An owner or driver at fault in a collision must pay for damage or injuries caused to another person under the financial-responsibility law. A reasonable possibility of civil liability after a crash can result in driving privileges being suspended for as long as three years. A financial settlement with the other crash parties may end the financial-responsibility suspension during its three-year period. The owner or driver must carry liability insurance under Alaska's mandatory-insurance law. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

lines.text: The manual lists bodily-injury-or-death liability limits of fifty thousand dollars and one hundred thousand dollars
but does not distinguish the application of those two limits in this paragraph.

narration.text: The manual lists bodily-injury-or-death liability limits of fifty thousand dollars and one hundred thousand dollars but does not distinguish the application of those two limits in this paragraph. The listed minimum property-damage liability coverage is twenty-five thousand dollars. Proof of liability insurance must be carried in the vehicle. Failure to show an officer proof of liability insurance can lead to a traffic citation or impoundment of the vehicle. The manual's insurance-law paragraph requires proof to DMV within fifteen days after a crash involving injury, death or property damage exceeding five hundred one dollars. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

lines.text: All drivers involved in a qualifying crash must provide insurance proof, even a driver who
did not cause the collision.

narration.text: All drivers involved in a qualifying crash must provide insurance proof, even a driver who did not cause the collision. The DMV insurance notification is separate from a report to police or to an insurance company. An investigating officer normally supplies an insurance-certificate form, and the form is also available from DMV offices or the state website. Being uninsured or missing the fifteen-day proof deadline results in a ninety-day suspension for a first occurrence and a one-year suspension for a second occurrence, according to the manual. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

narration.text: After any crash, stop immediately and move the vehicle out of traffic if doing so is possible. Warn approaching traffic after a crash; use flares or other road signals at night and avoid stepping in front of vehicles. Help injured people after a crash, arrange an ambulance when needed and move an injured person only when necessary. The crash guidance says to control serious bleeding and keep the injured person warm. Exchange names, addresses, driver-license and plate numbers, telephone numbers and insurance-company names with other drivers after a crash. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

narration.text: Record the identities of as many crash witnesses as possible. For a crash involving injury or at least two thousand dollars in total property damage within a municipality, immediately call local police using nine-one-one. For the same injury or damage circumstances outside a municipality, immediately contact Alaska State Troopers. Cooperate with the officer investigating a collision. The manual requires a DMV crash report within ten days, except when a police officer investigated the crash. A DMV crash report may be submitted electronically or by using the crash-report form available at DMV offices or on its website. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

narration.text: Moving-violation convictions receive point values from two through ten, with more crash-prone violations receiving higher values. Accumulating twelve points within twelve months or eighteen points within twenty-four months requires suspension or revocation despite personal hardship. A points-based suspension or revocation does not offer a limited work-purpose license. Drivers receive a warning when they reach half the point total that triggers suspension. Violation-free driving and completion of a defensive-driving course can earn point credits; the course may be used for point reduction once in twelve months.
